arguments.rule_content:
rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic Cobalt Strike beacons based on packing and entropy"
        author = "SOC Team"
        false_positive = "Packed .NET assemblies, legitimate Microsoft updates"
        remediation = "Refine entropy thresholds and add certificate checks"
    strings:
        $s1 = "beacon" wide ascii
        $s2 = { 60 00 73 00 76 00 63 00 68 00 6F 00 73 00 74 } // "svchost" in wide
        $x1 = { 4D 5A } // PE header
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and 
        filesize < 500KB and 
        entropy(0, filesize) > 7.0 and 
        all of ($s*)
}
// RECOMMENDATION: Modify to exclude signed binaries with valid Microsoft certificates

rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic Cobalt Strike beacon patterns in memory or files"
        author = "SOC Team"
        confidence = "medium"
        false_positives = "Packed .NET assemblies, legitimate Microsoft binaries"
        remediation = "Whitelist known-good hashes exhibiting this pattern"

    strings:
        $a = { 60 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 } // MZ header with padding
        $b = "beacon" wide ascii
        $c = "stager" wide ascii
        $d = { FF E0 } // jmp eax

    condition:
        all of ($a, $b, $c) or ($a and $d)
}

arguments.summary: A critical APT activity incident was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14), attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon). The compromise began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, leading to the deployment of a ShadowPad variant via rundll32.exe from the Temp directory. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23 and exhibited lateral movement attempts via SMB. Host-based indicators include mutex 'Global\APT41_ShadowPad_2026' and DNS queries to suspicious domains. Immediate containment actions included blocking C2 IPs at the firewall and resetting the user's credentials. A secondary Linux threat was also detected on a different host during post-containment scanning.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from User Temp Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '%TEMP%'
      - '%AppData%'
      - '%LocalAppData%'
  filter:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'advpack.dll'
      - 'iernonce.dll'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers
  - Admin scripts
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign led to the compromise of a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious macro in Outlook, resulting in execution of a ShadowPad variant attributed to APT-41. The attacker established C2 communication, attempted Kerberos TGT requests, and performed lateral movement via SMB. Immediate containment actions included user credential reset, full host scan, and execution of remediation playbook.

rundll32.exe loaded malicious beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011)
IDS detected Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001)
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 (T1558.001 - potential credential access)
SMB access to file server WS-FIN-050 (T1021.002 - lateral movement)
Initial alert generated for APT activity
EDR confirmed malicious process tree and network connections
Sandbox analysis attributed malware to APT-41 (ShadowPad variant)
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA reset completed
Full EPP scan completed; 1 threat detected and logged
Ansible remediation playbook executed successfully on WS-FIN-042

arguments.summary: A critical APT intrusion was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14), attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon). The attack began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell script from Outlook, leading to the execution of a ShadowPad variant via rundll32 from the Temp directory. The malware established a C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS and performed lateral movement attempts via SMB. Immediate containment actions included blocking the source and C2 IPs at the firewall and resetting the compromised user's credentials. The endpoint scan returned no threats, indicating evasion capabilities.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook.exe.
Encoded PowerShell command executed as child of Outlook (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded malicious beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011).
IDS triggered on Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 traffic to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Failed Kerberos TGT request indicating potential credential access attempt (T1558.001).
SMB access to file server WS-FIN-050 indicating lateral movement (T1021.002).
SOC analyst escalated alert to incident 'INC-AP2-V2'.
Firewall rules deployed to block source IP 10.0.5.14 and C2 IP 198.51.100.23.
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA token reset via IAM system.
Endpoint scan initiated on WS-FIN-042; returned no detections.

arguments.summary: Initial ransomware alert triggered by mass encryption behavior was determined to be a false positive. The activity was caused by a legitimate VeraCrypt-derived encryption utility used for backup purposes. No malicious intent or compromise was found. The alert was generated due to overly broad detection logic that flags any rapid encryption of files as ransomware.

EDR/NDR investigation initiated. Suspicious process chain identified: outlook.exe → powershell.exe (encoded) → rundll32.exe → beacon.dll.
Sandbox analysis completed. File 'restore_tool.exe' (hash: c7d8e9f...) classified as legitimate VeraCrypt-derivative utility (v7.2.1). No ransom note, C2, or malicious behaviors observed.
SIEM correlation confirmed user CORP\jsmith initiated legitimate backup encryption workflow. No evidence of lateral movement or credential misuse.
Incident reclassified as false positive. No containment actions taken.

title: Mass File Encryption - High Entropy
id: 5a7b8c9d-0e1f-2a3b-4c5d-6e7f8a9b0c1d
status: test
description: Detects rapid encryption of multiple files with high entropy, excluding known legitimate tools.
references:

author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 11
        Image: '*\\encrypt.exe'
        Entropy|float: > 7.8
    filter:
        Image|endswith: 
            - '\\veracrypt.exe'
            - '\\restore_tool.exe'
            - '\\cipher.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter
level: informational

Incident response actions completed: C2 blocked at firewall, beacon.dll removed, user CORP\jsmith disabled.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Mass Encryption Not by Known Legitimate Tools
id: 9a3b4d5e-6f7g-8h9i-0j1k-2l3m4n5o6p7q
status: experimental
description: Detects mass file encryption operations NOT performed by known legitimate encryption software.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        operation: 'FileWrite'
        entropy: 'high'
        extension: ('.aes', '.enc', '.locked')
    filter:
        image|contains: ('VeraCrypt.exe', 'BitLocker.exe', 'encrypt_tool.exe')
    condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate backup encryption jobs
level: high

arguments.summary: A critical ransomware alert was triggered by the detection of mass file encryption activity from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14). Investigation revealed the execution of 'restore_tool.exe' (SHA256: c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8), which was initially flagged by a heuristic rule. Further analysis determined the binary to be a legitimate VeraCrypt-derivative encryption utility used for backup purposes. However, the host was compromised via a phishing email leading to a Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. The beacon performed reconnaissance, modified the hosts file, and attempted lateral movement. No actual ransomware payload was executed. The alert severity was downgraded to informational based on sandbox analysis. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP, resetting the user's credentials, and remediating the host via automated playbook.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook.exe on WS-FIN-042.
Outlook spawned a hidden, encoded PowerShell process (T1566.001).
PowerShell created a malicious DLL 'beacon.dll' in the user's Temp directory.
rundll32.exe loaded 'beacon.dll', establishing a Cobalt Strike C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 on port 443 (T1218.011, T1071.001).
Hosts file was modified, likely to block security updates or redirect traffic (T1565.001).
IDS generated a critical alert for Cobalt Strike beacon C2 activity.
Failed Kerberos TGT request observed, indicating potential credential access attempts.
Successful SMB access to file server 10.0.5.50, indicating lateral movement (T1021.002).
Heuristic-based alert fired for 'restore_tool.exe' performing mass encryption, initially classified as critical ransomware.
Sandbox analysis completed, reclassifying 'restore_tool.exe' as a legitimate encryption tool (Veracrypt derivative).
Containment: Firewall rule deployed to block C2 IP 198.51.100.23.
Containment: User CORP\jsmith's password and MFA token were reset.
Remediation: Automated playbook executed to remove malware artifacts and harden the host.
Incident severity downgraded to 'informational' following root cause analysis.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_DLL
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident Cobalt Strike beacons based on known configuration patterns and artifacts."
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2"
    strings:
        $config_start = { 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 } // Common beacon config padding
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.0" fullword ascii
        $http_post = "POST / HTTP/1.0" fullword ascii
        $user_agent = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; Trident/7.0; rv:11.0) like Gecko" fullword ascii
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and // MZ Header
        $config_start and ($http_get or $http_post) and $user_agent
}

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign led to a Cobalt Strike beacon execution on a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious PowerShell launched from Outlook. The attacker attempted credential theft, lateral movement via SMB, and C2 communication over HTTPS. Containment actions included blocking the C2 IP, resetting the user's credentials, and executing a full remediation playbook. Sandbox analysis initially underestimated the threat due to limited telemetry, but timeline reconstruction confirmed post-exploitation activity.

timeline.description: User 'CORP\jsmith' launched Outlook (initial access vector suspected).
Malicious PowerShell executed with hidden window and encoded command, spawned by Outlook.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 over TCP/443.
IDS triggered on 'ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity' signature.
Failed Kerberos TGT request indicates attempted credential brute-force or AS-REP roast.
Successful SMB access to file server 10.0.3.10, confirming lateral movement.
Post-exploitation alert generated; incident formally escalated.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 10.0.5.14 (C2 server).
User 'CORP\jsmith' credentials (password and MFA) reset; secure enrollment link issued.
Ansible remediation playbook 'remediate_cobalt_strike.yml' executed successfully on WS-FIN-042.

arguments.summary: Post-exploitation activity detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14) under user CORP\jsmith. Initial access achieved via phishing email triggering encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook. The attacker deployed a malicious DLL using rundll32.exe from the Temp directory, establishing C2 communication with a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) over HTTPS. Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to internal servers. The sample 'taskeng_monitor.exe' analyzed in sandbox showed limited activity but omitted critical behaviors such as LSASS memory dumping and WMI-based execution on a domain controller. Detection occurred through EDR alerts on suspicious process chains and SIEM correlation of Cobalt Strike beaconing. Response actions included password and MFA reset for the compromised user, full host scan (which detected a Linux dropper in cron), and application of CIS hardening playbook to the affected workstation.

        $c2_get = "/index.php?css=load" wide ascii
    condition:
        any of ($ua*) and $c2_get

The root cause appears to be a phishing compromise of the finance user jsmith@corp.local.
